html:
Copena was a Middle Woodland culture of the middle Tennessee River valley in northern Alabama, with sites reaching into Tennessee and Georgia. On this map it covers about 100 BCE to 500 CE. The name joins the first letters of copper and galena, two materials found in its burials.

Copena people buried their dead in earth mounds and in caves, often with copper ornaments, galena (a shiny lead ore), mica and stone pipes. These goods came along the trade routes of the Hopewell world. Their neighbours included the Miller people to the west and the Swift Creek people to the southeast. Much of what is known comes from mounds dug in the 1930s, before new dams flooded parts of the valley.
